title: How Azad University Affects Your Academic Future
excerpt: A very important thing nobody tells you about Azad University

blocks.text: The Effects Azad University Will Have on the Rest of Your Academic Path
A very important thing that nobody tells you about Azad University is that starting your studies at Azad University takes away some of your opportunities in your academic path.
I'll get straight to the point:

If your GPA at Azad University is 16.5 or 17 (I don't remember exactly) or above, you can go from bachelor's to master's without the Konkur and continue your studies - at Azad universities themselves.

But there is also a general talented students plan that is issued by the Ministry of Science. For example, you are the top student at Azad University and you want to go study at a state university. Why? Because first of all you shouldn't pay money and it's free, and in terms of rank it's better!

Now one of the ways you have is this talented students plan. The Ministry of Science itself in the directive it issues says, sir, if your GPA is above 17 and you are among the top 3% of your own incoming class, you are covered by the talented students plan and you can apply to any university in Iran, whether Azad or state, and participate in this plan.
Let me also say this point that this talented students plan is completely competitive, meaning your participation in this plan does not mean your final acceptance.

But what's the story? The story is that state universities give their own exceptions and put limitations on the Ministry of Science directive. For example, the most important one is that: Azad University students cannot participate in this plan.
Unfortunately, year by year this is increasing and this limitation is growing more for Azad University.
Is it fair? No it's not. Definitely not.

But the story doesn't end here. If you are at the master's level too - if you are at a state university too - if you are first at this state university too - and you want to use this talented students possibility for the PhD level, again for some universities you can't. Why? It's very ridiculous! Because your bachelor's was at Azad University!
Yeah, anyway, this story is not fair and just at all but it exists and it's good that you know about it :)
